title: Why GTA 6 Should Borrow Core Elements From GTA 4
description: Revisiting GTA 4 from 2008, gaming critics discuss the groundbreaking physics and immersive details Rockstar should bring back to GTA 6 for ultimate realism.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## The Timeless Appeal of GTA 4

As the anticipation for Grand Theft Auto 6 reaches fever pitch, players and critics alike are reflecting on what made previous entries in the franchise so special. Recently revisiting Grand Theft Auto 4 for the first time since its 2008 release highlights just how many incredible features and atmospheric details exist in that game—features that many fans hope Rockstar Games will borrow and modernize for GTA 6.

While Grand Theft Auto 5 delivered a massive sandbox and immense commercial success, it noticeably dialed back some of the gritty realism and groundbreaking physics that defined Niko Bellic's adventure in Liberty City.

### Bringing Back the Euphoria Physics Engine

One of the most striking aspects of GTA 4 was its implementation of the Euphoria physics engine. The weight of the vehicles, the unpredictable and realistic pedestrian reactions, and the way bodies interacted with the environment made the world feel genuinely alive. Driving in GTA 4 demanded respect and skill, thanks to realistic suspension and momentum models.

In contrast, GTA 5 opted for a more accessible, arcade-like driving experience and simplified physics to cater to a broader audience. While this suited the sunny, fast-paced satire of Los Santos, it left some purists longing for the tactical depth and grounded feel of the 2008 classic.

### What GTA 6 Can Learn From the Past

As Vice City and the broader state of Leonida prepare to open their doors in GTA 6, Rockstar has the opportunity to marry the epic scale of modern hardware with the meticulous attention to detail of the past. Fans are crossing their fingers for deeper environmental interactions, more intelligent NPC behaviors, and driving mechanics that offer a genuine sense of weight and consequence.

## Editor's Take

GTA 5 proved Rockstar's mastery of the modern blockbuster, but GTA 4 remains a masterclass in immersive detail and physics. If GTA 6 successfully blends the gritty realism of 2008 with next-generation scale, it won't just be a hit—it will redefine open-world gaming for a decade.
